definitions.explanation: A romantic meeting or rendezvous, especially one that is secret or clandestine. Carries a literary, poetic nuance.

examples.japanese: ⟦{二人|ふたり}→二人：00622_futari⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{逢瀬|おうせ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{重|かさ}ねた→重ねる：02039_kasaneru⟧。
examples.english: The two met in secret again and again.

examples.japanese: ⟦{人目|ひとめ}→人目：17973_hitome⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{忍|しの}んで→忍ぶ：16953_shinobu⟧{逢瀬|おうせ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{楽|たの}しんでいた→楽しむ：01203_tanoshimu⟧。
examples.english: They enjoyed their secret meetings away from prying eyes.

examples.japanese: ⟦{小説|しょうせつ}→小説：01434_shousetsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{主人公|しゅじんこう}→主人公：11404_shujinkou⟧たち⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{月明|つきあ}かり→月明かり：05047_tsukiakari⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{下|もと}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{逢瀬|おうせ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{果|は}たし→果たす：10060_hatasu⟧、⟦{互|たが}い→互い：03402_tagai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{想|おも}い⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{確|たし}かめ{合|あ}った。
examples.english: The protagonists of the novel had their rendezvous by moonlight and confirmed their feelings for each other.

notes:
USAGE: {逢瀬|おうせ} is a literary and poetic word. It is rarely used in everyday conversation but appears frequently in novels, period dramas, and romantic literature. In casual speech, ⟦{密会|みっかい}→密会：25485_mikkai⟧ (secret meeting) or simply ⟦デート→デート：03861_deeto⟧ would be used instead.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {逢瀬|おうせ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{重|かさ}ねる→重ねる：02039_kasaneru⟧ (to meet in secret repeatedly)
- {逢瀬|おうせ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{楽|たの}しむ→楽しむ：01203_tanoshimu⟧ (to enjoy a tryst)
- {逢瀬|おうせ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{果|は}たす→果たす：10060_hatasu⟧ (to carry out a rendezvous)
- ⟦{人目|ひとめ}→人目：17973_hitome⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{忍|しの}んで→忍ぶ：16953_shinobu⟧{逢瀬|おうせ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧... (to meet secretly away from prying eyes)

The kanji {逢|おう} means "to meet" (a more literary variant of ⟦{会|あ}う→会う：00482_au⟧) and {瀬|せ} means "shallows" or "opportunity," giving the compound a sense of a fleeting, precious encounter.
